# NeMo Switchyard routes — routing IN FRONT OF LiteLLM, additive and bypassable.
#
# MIGRATED to switchyard-server 0.3.0 on 2026-09-23 (was 0.2.0). Checked with the 0.3.0 binary:
# `--dry-run` clean with no warnings, auto-local/direct-27b answered, and the 0.3.0 server escalated
# 3 of 4 hard prompts where the live 0.2.0 escalated 0 of 4. What changed from 0.2.0:
#   - forward_auth now works (0.2.0 rejected it), so this server no longer holds a key — see below.
#   - capable_/efficient_system_prompt on a route are gone (rejected as unknown fields); per-tier
#     steering is a target `system_prompt`. See the *-auto targets and the routes note.
# The 0.2.0 file is what the README's "What the docs get wrong about 0.2.0" describes; that section
# is history now — `type = "auto"`, target system_prompt/reasoning_effort and forward_auth all exist.
#
# Every target is an EXISTING LiteLLM alias from inference/litellm/config.yaml, reached on the
# ai-lab bus as http://litellm:4000/v1. LiteLLM keeps credentials, aliasing, caching, spend
# tracking and its exporters. Switchyard only decides WHICH alias serves a call.
#
# BYPASS IS THE DEFAULT, NOT A MODE:
#   1. Port level  — LiteLLM still owns :4000 and is untouched. Anything pointed there never sees
#                    this file. Routing is opt-in by calling :4010.
#   2. Route level — the `direct-*` passthroughs below pin one model with no routing decision.
schema_version = 1

# ── upstream ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# forward_auth = true (works in 0.3.0; 0.2.0 rejected the key, which is why this file used
# api_key_env and the container held LITELLM_MASTER_KEY). The caller's own Authorization header is
# forwarded to LiteLLM, which does the validating: measured 2026-09-23 against 0.3.0 with NO key in
# the container — no credential -> 401, wrong key -> 401, a valid key -> answered. That closes the
# hole documented in docker-compose.yml (an unauthenticated peer getting master-key-backed
# completions). Consequences: every caller of :4010 must now send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`;
# /health, /metrics and /v1/models stay unauthenticated (route ids only). Classifier judge calls
# use the same forwarded credential.
[llm_clients.litellm]
format = "openai_chat"
base_url = "http://litellm:4000/v1"
forward_auth = true
max_retries = 2

# ── targets: existing router aliases, nothing new ───────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.2.0 targets accept ONLY id / llm_client / extra_body. `system_prompt` and `reasoning_effort`
# are documented but rejected — per-tier steering goes on the ROUTE instead (see below).
[targets.lightning]
id = "nemotron-lightning"          # Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B NVFP4 (QAD) — efficient tier
llm_client = "litellm"

[targets.qwen-27b-1m]
id = "qwen3.8-27b-1m"              # 256K ctx + MTP — the capable tier that is up today
llm_client = "litellm"

# auto-local's tiers: same model ids as the two above, plus the tier prompt (see routes note below).
# OWN CLIENT, same URL, on purpose: target identity is (model id, llm_client), so reusing `litellm` would
# make Switchyard keep one target per id and silently DROP the other (WARN only) — the prompt would vanish.
[llm_clients.litellm_auto]
format = "openai_chat"
base_url = "http://litellm:4000/v1"
forward_auth = true
max_retries = 2

[targets.lightning-auto]
id = "nemotron-lightning"
llm_client = "litellm_auto"
system_prompt = "Answer directly and finish the task. If it needs multi-step planning or wide code edits, say so briefly instead of guessing."

[targets.qwen-27b-auto]
id = "qwen3.8-27b-1m"
llm_client = "litellm_auto"
system_prompt = "You were escalated to because a smaller model stopped short. Read what it already did and continue; do not redo settled work."

[targets.flash-next]
id = "qwen3.8-flash-next"          # SGLang custom build; start inference/sglang-flashnext first
llm_client = "litellm"

[targets.omni]
id = "nemotron-omni"               # always-on multimodal engine, own card
llm_client = "litellm"

# JUDGE CLIENT — kept as the REVERT PATH. History: the 0.2.0 build shipped with the judge at
# nemotron-omni because lightning-as-judge produced parse_error (reasoning model spent its budget
# thinking and returned EMPTY content -> confidence 0.000 -> silent fall-through to efficient).
# 2026-09-13 the classifier target was switched to lightning ON PURPOSE: the hypothesis is that
# the old failures were reasoning-budget exhaustion (thinking ON by default) rather than a model
# choice, and thinking is now OFF by default for lightning in inference/litellm/config.yaml (chat_template_kwargs
# enable_thinking: false on the nemotron-lightning alias AND the switchyard group's efficient tier), so the judge verdict arrives as plain text. Target identity is (model id, llm_client):
# this judge target (nemotron-omni, litellm_judge) stays distinct from every answer target.
[llm_clients.litellm_judge]
format = "openai_chat"
base_url = "http://litellm:4000/v1"
forward_auth = true
max_retries = 2

[targets.judge]
id = "nemotron-omni"
llm_client = "litellm_judge"

# TWO CLUSTER LANES. BOTH ARE MULTIMODAL — text+image in, 1M ctx, GLM-5.3 Flash on the cluster
# behind a remote gateway. The gateway's "text-only lane" naming for glm-5.3-flash is WRONG:
# measured 2026-09-14 through this router, it named the colour of solid PNGs correctly and it
# returns tool_calls and streams. Neither of these is a text-only lane; do not re-label them.
#
# Either engine may be stopped at any time — normal here, not a config fault, so this file does
# not record which is up. Declaring both (rather than deleting a stopped one) means each starts
# working again with no edit here, the convention inference/litellm/config.yaml already uses for
# deepseek-v4-flash.
[targets.cluster-glm]
id = "cluster/glm-5.3-flash"       # cluster TP4, 1M ctx, text+image in — remote, over the fabric
llm_client = "litellm"

[targets.cluster-glm-next]
id = "cluster/glm-5.3-flash-next"  # cluster TP4, 1M ctx, text+image in — remote, over the fabric
llm_client = "litellm"

# ── routed models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# type = "stage_router" spelled out: 0.2.0 rejects the documented `type = "auto"` preset, so its
# documented values (picker = efficient_first, confidence_threshold = 0.5) are written here.
# Start on the efficient tier; escalate to capable on tool-ACTIVITY signals (not on the mere
# presence of tool definitions — measured 2026-09-13).
#
# handoff_notes.escalation_note is the quality field that was missing from the first build. Without
# it the capable tier inherits the conversation with no idea it is a second attempt, and re-does
# work the efficient tier already did. The wording mirrors NVIDIA's own LiteLLM example.
# Per-tier steering is a per-TARGET `system_prompt` since 0.3.0 (it was the route-level
# capable_/efficient_system_prompt on 0.2.0, which 0.3.0 rejects). The auto-local tiers get their OWN
# targets (`*-auto`, same model id and client) because a target's prompt applies wherever it serves a
# completion — putting it on `lightning` / `qwen-27b-1m` would also steer the direct-* A/B baselines.

# PRIMARY. Fully local: no egress, no remote dependency. Trust this one when the fabric is down.
[routes.auto-local]
id = "auto-local"
type = "stage_router"
capable_target = "qwen-27b-auto"
efficient_target = "lightning-auto"
picker = "efficient_first"
confidence_threshold = 0.5
recent_turn_window = 3
context_window = 262144
tool_calling = true
reasoning = true
handoff_notes = { escalation_note = "A smaller model handled the earlier turns and did not finish. Continue from its work rather than restarting it." }

# WITHOUT THIS BLOCK THE ROUTE NEVER ESCALATES. stage_router computes no confidence of its own —
# with no classifier every request reports
#   x-model-router-rationale: fall-through selected <efficient> (confidence 0.000)
# and efficient_first falls through unconditionally. That is not a tuning problem, it is a missing
# component: measured over hundreds of calls, the capable tier had NEVER served a request.
[routes.auto-local.classifier]
# `lightning-auto`, not `lightning`: a route may not hold the same model id on two clients, and the
# efficient tier is on litellm_auto. Judge calls do NOT receive the target prompt.
target = "lightning-auto"
base_threshold = 0.5
max_output_tokens = 4096

# Same pair, capable tier on the flashnext engine. Only works while that engine is up.
[routes.auto-flashnext]
id = "auto-flashnext"
type = "stage_router"
capable_target = "flash-next"
efficient_target = "lightning"
picker = "efficient_first"
confidence_threshold = 0.5
recent_turn_window = 3
tool_calling = true
reasoning = true
handoff_notes = { escalation_note = "A smaller model handled the earlier turns and did not finish. Continue from its work rather than restarting it." }

# WITHOUT THIS BLOCK THE ROUTE NEVER ESCALATES — same missing-component story as above.
[routes.auto-flashnext.classifier]
target = "lightning"
base_threshold = 0.5
max_output_tokens = 4096

# Local efficient tier, capable tier on your own cluster. Crosses the fabric, not the internet.
[routes.auto-cluster]
id = "auto-cluster"
type = "stage_router"
capable_target = "cluster-glm"
efficient_target = "lightning"
picker = "efficient_first"
confidence_threshold = 0.5
recent_turn_window = 3
context_window = 1000000
tool_calling = true
reasoning = true
handoff_notes = { escalation_note = "A smaller model handled the earlier turns and did not finish. Continue from its work rather than restarting it." }

# WITHOUT THIS BLOCK THE ROUTE NEVER ESCALATES — same missing-component story as above.
[routes.auto-cluster.classifier]
target = "lightning"
base_threshold = 0.5
max_output_tokens = 4096

# A frontier-API capable tier is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: it needs a second llm_clients block with a
# real egress path and an API key — an egress-allowlist and secret-handling change, not a config
# tweak. See README.md "Adding a frontier tier".

# ── explicit bypasses ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One passthrough per tier that appears in a route above, so every routed model can be A/B'd
# against its own tiers ON THE SAME SURFACE. That is the only honest way to tell whether routing
# is helping, and it is why direct-flashnext and direct-cluster exist rather than just the two
# the first build shipped.
[routes.direct-lightning]
id = "direct-lightning"
type = "passthrough"
target = "lightning"

[routes.direct-27b]
id = "direct-27b"
type = "passthrough"
target = "qwen-27b-1m"

[routes.direct-flashnext]
id = "direct-flashnext"
type = "passthrough"
target = "flash-next"

[routes.direct-cluster]
id = "direct-cluster"
type = "passthrough"
target = "cluster-glm"

# The -next engine, addressable on its own. Same capability as direct-cluster — a separate
# checkpoint on the gateway, NOT a different modality. When its engine is stopped the upstream
# error names the backend directly ("Cannot connect to host 192.0.2.12:8000"), which is the
# quickest way to tell "engine not started" apart from a genuinely missing model id.
[routes.direct-cluster-next]
id = "direct-cluster-next"
type = "passthrough"
target = "cluster-glm-next"

[routes.direct-omni]
id = "direct-omni"
type = "passthrough"
target = "omni"

# VALIDATE THIS FILE WITH THE PLUGIN, NOT WITH switchyard-server 0.2.0.
# Those are different builds — the server is the v0.2.0 TAG, the Relay plugin is built from a main
# COMMIT — and their schemas differ. Measured 2026-09-13: 0.2.0 happily accepts
# capable_system_prompt / efficient_system_prompt on a stage_router; the plugin REJECTS both with
# "unknown field", and the gateway then refuses to start with "plugin activation failed". Using the
# server as a proxy validator passed a file the plugin could not load. It does accept handoff_notes.
# The authoritative check is starting the gateway:
#   nemo-relay gateway start    # config errors surface AFTER the banner, so read the whole output
#
# Switchyard deployment for the NeMo Relay NATIVE PLUGIN (host-side).
#
# Same schema_version-1 language as inference/switchyard/routes.toml — the Relay plugin and
# switchyard-server deliberately share one config format ("The plugin does not define a second
# routing or target configuration language"). It is a SEPARATE FILE anyway, for two reasons:
#
# 1. ADDRESS. Relay runs on the HOST, so the router is 127.0.0.1:4000. The server's copy runs in a
#    container on the ai-lab bus and uses http://litellm:4000. Same router, different address.
#
# 2. WIRE FORMAT. The Relay plugin does NOT translate between provider APIs:
#      "Each route's target client must use the caller's wire format ... The runner selects the
#       upstream backend from that format rather than translating a route to a different provider
#       API. When one upstream model must serve multiple caller formats, declare a target and
#       route for each corresponding client format."
#    switchyard-server DOES translate (verified: its /v1/messages accepts Anthropic and speaks
#    openai_chat upstream). The plugin does not. Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages, so the
#    clients here are `anthropic_messages` — pointed at LiteLLM's own Anthropic surface, verified
#    2026-09-13: POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/messages returns a well-formed
#    {"type":"message","stop_reason":"end_turn"}.
#
# A model name Relay sees that is NOT a route id below is passed through to Relay's continuation
# unchanged, so this cannot capture traffic it was not configured for.
schema_version = 1

[llm_clients.litellm_anthropic]
format = "anthropic_messages"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4000"
api_key_env = "LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
max_retries = 2

[targets.lightning]
id = "nemotron-lightning"
llm_client = "litellm_anthropic"

[targets.qwen-27b-1m]
id = "qwen3.8-27b-1m"
llm_client = "litellm_anthropic"

# Routed model. Claude Code would be pointed at this id.
[routes.auto-local]
id = "auto-local"
type = "stage_router"
capable_target = "qwen-27b-1m"
efficient_target = "lightning"
picker = "efficient_first"
confidence_threshold = 0.5
recent_turn_window = 3
context_window = 262144
tool_calling = true
reasoning = true
handoff_notes = { escalation_note = "A smaller model handled the earlier turns and did not finish. Continue from its work rather than restarting it." }

[routes.direct-lightning]
id = "direct-lightning"
type = "passthrough"
# Real engine window; also what relay-claude exports as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS.
context_window = 262144
target = "lightning"

[routes.direct-27b]
id = "direct-27b"
type = "passthrough"
# Real engine window; also what relay-claude exports as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS.
context_window = 262144
target = "qwen-27b-1m"

# ── JUDGE, so auto-local ESCALATES on this path too ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Without a classifier stage_router computes no confidence: turn 1 is always the efficient tier
# and nothing else can move it. The standalone :4010 server has had this judge since the fix that
# made it escalate; the Relay plugin was left without one because its schema was stricter than the
# server's and rejected other route fields. It ACCEPTS this block — verified 2026-09-14 by starting
# the gateway against a copy. Same judge, same threshold, so the two surfaces route alike.
# Own client despite the identical URL: target identity is (model id, llm_client), and a collision
# silently DROPS one target with only a WARN.
[llm_clients.litellm_judge]
format = "anthropic_messages"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4000"
api_key_env = "LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
max_retries = 2

# JUDGE CLIENT, openai_chat on purpose. The classifier judge is nemotron-lightning with thinking
# OFF (inference/litellm/config.yaml, chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking: false on the alias).
# That switch only reaches the vLLM engine on the OpenAI wire: LiteLLM's /v1/messages translation
# DROPS chat_template_kwargs, so on anthropic_messages lightning keeps reasoning, burns the token
# budget and returns an empty/truncated verdict (parse_error -> confidence 0.000 -> silent
# fall-through to the efficient tier — the exact failure the omni judge was meant to cure).
# Measured 2026-09-14 over 6 hard prompts through a throwaway gateway: anthropic judge escalated
# 1/6, this openai judge escalated 5/6 (matching :4010), 0 judge failures. So the classifier speaks
# openai_chat to :4000/v1 even though the answer tiers above speak anthropic_messages; the plugin
# accepts the mixed formats (--dry-run OK, gateway verified).
[llm_clients.litellm_judge_oai]
format = "openai_chat"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1"
api_key_env = "LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
max_retries = 2

# ACTIVE judge: nemotron-lightning over the openai_chat client, so thinking-off actually applies.
# id is the `nemotron-lightning-judge` LiteLLM alias (same engine, thinking off), NOT `nemotron-lightning`:
# the Switchyard 0.3.0 plugin refuses a route that holds one model id on two wire formats, and this
# judge is openai_chat while the answer tier `lightning` above is anthropic_messages. The alias is
# defined in inference/litellm/config.yaml. (0.2.0-era plugin accepted the shared id.)
[targets.judge-lightning]
id = "nemotron-lightning-judge"
llm_client = "litellm_judge_oai"

# REVERT PATH, unreferenced. nemotron-omni over the anthropic client. omni is more robust than
# lightning on the anthropic wire (it does not reason itself into an empty verdict as often), so if
# the openai-judge path ever regresses, `target = "judge"` restores a working — if slower — judge.
[targets.judge]
id = "nemotron-omni"

[routes.auto-local.classifier]

version = 1

[[plugins.dynamic]]
manifest = "/home/user/.local/share/nemo-relay-plugins/switchyard-0.3.0/relay-plugin.toml"

# Switchyard deployment. schema_version-1 TOML, the SAME language switchyard-server reads.
# Host-side copy: Relay runs on the host so the router is 127.0.0.1:4000, and its clients must be
# anthropic_messages because the plugin does NOT translate wire formats.
[plugins.dynamic.config]
priority = 0
switchyard_config_path = "/home/user/lab/clients/nemo-relay/routes.toml"

# Require a real signature rather than the integrity_only downgrade. The bundle is signed and this
# key is verified against it (authenticity_state=valid; a wrong key is rejected). integrity_only
# would let anyone who can write the plugin directory rewrite the .so AND its sha256 together.
[plugins.policy.defaults]
attestation = "signature_required"
trusted_public_keys = ["ed25519:rASDTu8lHF/D+tIowmL7Tpu2pOPDzmN+NrC8FZdO+aM="]

enabled = true

mode = "append"

enabled = true
agent_name = "lab"

filename_template = "nemo-relay-atif-{session_id}.json"

# ── OTLP EXPORT TO THE LAB COLLECTOR (added 2026-09-15) ─────────────────────────────────────
# Metrics -> otel-collector :4318 -> Prometheus (OTLP receiver) -> Grafana "AI Lab — NeMo Relay Routing".
# Traces  -> otel-collector -> Tempo + Phoenix (project "nemo-relay" via the collector transform).
# gen_ai projection on purpose: it omits messages and tool payloads, matching the lab rule that prompt
# content is not exported (observability/README.md). Metrics carry labels only, never content.
# Logs deliberately OFF: every llm.chunk and hook mark would become a LogRecord, and hook marks carry
# prompt text. service_name becomes the Prometheus `job` label (the board's $relay_job).
[components.config.opentelemetry]
enabled = true

[[components.config.opentelemetry.endpoints]]
type = "gen_ai"
endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces"
transport = "http_binary"
service_name = "nemo-relay"

[components.config.opentelemetry.metrics]
enabled = true
# Metrics endpoint is derived from the trace endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics.
# 15 s instead of the 60 s default so the 10 s-refresh board lags a scrape, not a minute.
export_interval_millis = 15000
